clue.text: Hitch and tie other side

parts.note: a tie is a drawn game, a draw
the back is the reverse or other side of something

explanation.surface: An instruction to hitch something up and tie it on the far side, like securing a load.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitch is a snag or disadvantage, and so is a drawback.

clue.text: Change be enough? Bankers to count on the other hand

parts.note: to do is to suffice, as in that will do

indicators.note: the banks of a word are its outer letters, here those of count

parts.note: or introduces an alternative, as on the other hand does

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about whether money men can be relied on to tally things up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bankers' looks like financiers but means the edges: CT, the two outer letters of 'count'.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor something is to alter or tamper with it, so change in the verb sense.

clue.text: American with his woman, perhaps overseas

parts.note: broad is American slang for a woman, perhaps a man's woman

explanation.surface: An American and his partner travelling abroad, perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: To be abroad is to be in a foreign country, especially overseas.

clue.text: One helps you stop and live around playboy's house

indicators.note: around means the live word sits either side of the others

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
a rake is a playboy, and rake's gives RAKES

explanation.surface: Settling down and moving in around a playboy's mansion, someone who makes you stop partying.
explanation.definitionFit: A brake shoe is the curved block that presses on a wheel to slow and halt a vehicle.

clue.text: Supporting business, one is protected by Conservatives

indicators.note: being protected by means being surrounded by the other letters

parts.note: CON and TORY are both short words for a Conservative
a firm is a business
a means one

explanation.surface: A political line about a business backed and shielded by the Conservative party.
explanation.definitionFit: Confirmatory evidence is corroborating, lending support to something already stated.

clue.text: Too much work: left to retire

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the work and left letters are read backwards

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone complains of overwork and decides it is time to give up the job.
explanation.walkthrough: TROPPO is Italian for 'too much', familiar from the musical direction 'non troppo'; reversing OPPORT gives it.
explanation.definitionFit: Troppo is the Italian musical term meaning excessively, borrowed into English usage.

clue.text: Stand up to grab bottom of chain for flush

indicators.note: grabbing means holding a letter inside

parts.note: to rise is to stand up

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the last letter, here of chain

explanation.surface: Getting up to pull the chain of an old-fashioned toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To flush something is to rinse it out with a rush of water.

clue.text: Private planes not primarily for flying

indicators.note: flying means the letters are scattered and rearranged
without its first letter, so for loses its F

explanation.surface: A note that private aircraft are not mainly for flying, perhaps just for show.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal matters are private ones, concerning one individual and no one else.

clue.text: Pass with extra study

parts.note: over means extra or left over
to take a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: A student who passes thanks to additional revision.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtake another vehicle is to pass it on the road.

clue.text: The end of dog exercises, no lead on Rottweiler

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: no here means without, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: to train is to exercise or drill

indicators.note: the lead, or first letter, of Rottweiler

explanation.surface: A dog-walker's scene: the dog is exercised without its lead on, a risky business with a Rottweiler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like the dog's leash, but it means the first letter; TRAINS without that R is TAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtains is informal for the finish or death of something, as the theatre curtain falls at the close.

clue.text: Part of meal: English course's not first class

indicators.note: not here means without, so the named letters are removed

parts.note: Aintree is the racecourse near Liverpool that stages the Grand National
A1 means first class, read here as the letters A and I

explanation.surface: A meal planner observes that this English dish is not top of the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests a meal course but is a racecourse: AINTREE, home of the Grand National horse race, loses A1 (first class, with the 1 read as I) to leave NTREE.
explanation.definitionFit: An entrée is a dish served as one course of a meal, the main course in American usage.

clue.text: New couple getting away? Someone horny after some swapping

indicators.note: swapping letters about rearranges them into a new order

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of a randy partner after some partner-swapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Honeymooners are newlyweds who have gone away on holiday after their wedding.

clue.text: Speak over judge

parts.note: O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for an over
to rate is to assess or judge

explanation.surface: A command to address the court in preference to the judge.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to speak formally, making a speech, often pompously.

clue.text: Put right in print; did press at first?

indicators.note: at first places the pressing word before the print word

parts.note: to press clothes is to iron them, so did press is ironed
a book that is out has been published and is in print

explanation.surface: A printer's question: was the error corrected when the press first ran?
explanation.definitionFit: Ironing out problems is an idiom for resolving or correcting them, like smoothing creases.

clue.text: Bum ciggy, ultimately nick matches for smoker?

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means bad or faulty, so the letters are put wrong and rearranged
the final letter of ciggy

explanation.surface: Someone cadges a cigarette and then pinches some matches to light it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' reads as a verb, to cadge, but it is the anagram signal; Y from ciggy plus NICK and MATCHES rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimney stack belches smoke from a house, so the question mark marks it as a fanciful kind of smoker.

clue.text: Fake: tiny chest with boobs

indicators.note: boobs are blunders, so the letters are mistaken and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark about cosmetic surgery on a small chest.
explanation.definitionFit: Synthetic means artificial or man-made, so fake rather than natural.

clue.text: Faculty performing IT update

indicators.note: performing means putting on a turn, so the letters are acted out anew in another order

explanation.surface: A university faculty carrying out a computer system update.
explanation.definitionFit: An aptitude is a natural ability or talent, a faculty in that sense.

clue.text: Pierce upwards with hole in squash bottle

indicators.note: in means the bore and hole letters sit inside the squash word

parts.note: to jam is to squash or cram

indicators.note: in a down clue upwards means read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: to bore is to pierce
O is a hole by its shape

explanation.surface: Punching a hole upward into a bottle of squash, a fruit cordial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squash' looks like the drink but is the verb, JAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A jeroboam is a large wine bottle, holding about four standard bottles of champagne.

clue.text: Feeling hand over male partners during sex

parts.note: to present something is to hand it over formally

indicators.note: during means the partners word sits inside the sex word

parts.note: IT is a crossword staple for sex or sex appeal
Chambers gives man as a husband or male sexual partner, so men

explanation.surface: A racy line about emotion running high as men hand themselves over in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A presentiment is a foreboding, an intuitive feeling that something is about to happen.

clue.text: Cultured occasionally cheat in game

indicators.note: occasionally means every other letter is taken

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them

explanation.surface: A refined player is now and then caught cheating at a board game.
explanation.walkthrough: CLUEDO is the British name of the murder-mystery board game known as Clue in North America.
explanation.definitionFit: Cluedo is a classic board game in which players deduce who committed a murder.

clue.text: Stays in my place

parts.note: cor and my are both exclamations of surprise
to set something is to place it

explanation.surface: Someone remaining at the speaker's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stays' looks like a verb but is the noun: stays are the stiffened bands of a bodice. Cor is a British exclamation like 'gosh'.
explanation.definitionFit: A corset is a stiffened undergarment, traditionally called stays.

clue.text: So that till's working at the start

indicators.note: at the start places the working phrase ahead of the till word

parts.note: something in order is functioning properly, working
till means up to, as does to (from nine till five, nine to five)

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper checks the cash register is functioning before opening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'till' suggests a cash register, but it is the preposition, meaning until.
explanation.definitionFit: In order to introduces a purpose, the same job as so that does in a sentence.

clue.text: Small flyer climbs and drops

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means read upwards, reversed

parts.note: a bird is a flyer

explanation.surface: A little bird soars up and then dives.
explanation.definitionFit: Dribs are small drops or amounts, as in the phrase dribs and drabs.

clue.text: That man will love welcome

parts.note: that man will contracts to he'll
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A promise that a certain man will love the greeting he gets.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello is a greeting, the word said to welcome someone on arrival.

clue.text: More work in university subject with top grade for college

indicators.note: with this for that means one letter replaces another

parts.note: a topic is a subject of discussion
A is the top grade in exams

explanation.surface: A student grumbles about extra coursework in a subject, chasing a top grade to get into college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' looks like 'extra' but is Sir Thomas More, the Tudor statesman who wrote Utopia.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is the 1516 book by Thomas More describing an ideal island society.

clue.text: Down pop with son drinking last of Coke

indicators.note: drinking means taking a letter inside

parts.note: pop is informal for father

indicators.note: the last of something is its final part, so only the closing letter of Coke is used

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Dad and his boy share a fizzy drink, gulping the last of the Coke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down' looks like a verb, to drink, but it is the soft plumage of birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is the soft fine plumage of birds, made of small fluffy feathers.

clue.text: Catch up with nurse: hospital tackling chaos, mostly

parts.note: EN is an enrolled nurse

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a mess is chaos, disorder
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A busy ward: catching up with a nurse while the hospital deals with near chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: To enmesh is to entangle, as in a net, so someone enmeshed is caught up in something.

clue.text: Bully in quiet school determined to bite head of year

parts.note: P is piano, quiet in music

indicators.note: biting takes a letter between the teeth, so it goes inside
the head of something is its top or front, so only the opening letter of year is used

parts.note: out to do something means determined to do it

explanation.surface: A school scene: in a quiet corner, someone set on attacking the head of year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head of year' suggests a teacher, but it means just the first letter, Y, which goes after the S of SCH.
explanation.definitionFit: To psych out is to intimidate or unnerve an opponent, much as a bully does.
